prompt:
Create ONE native editable SVG artwork sheet containing TWELVE finished, individually usable small fantasy minion illustrations. Exact canvas 1920 by 1008, viewBox="0 0 1920 1008". Layout exactly FOUR columns by THREE rows, each cell exactly 480 by 336, no gutters, no visible labels. Each row holds TWO normal/Golden pairs, adjacent left to right. This is a shared-style sheet, not a comic or a UI mockup.

STRUCTURE: twelve separate top-level groups with these exact IDs and positions. Row 1 at y=0: squire-normal at x=0, squire-golden at x=480, pup-normal at x=960, pup-golden at x=1440. Row 2 at y=336: imp-normal at x=0, imp-golden at x=480, spark-normal at x=960, spark-golden at x=1440. Row 3 at y=672: cub-normal at x=0, cub-golden at x=480, wisp-normal at x=960, wisp-golden at x=1440. Give each group its own background rectangle and translate its local 480 by 336 scene into the grid. Keep every path within its own cell and every resource self-contained. Native static vector shapes/paths only; no raster images, scripts, external resources, text, fonts, logos or watermarks. No card border, statistics, tier symbols, medallions or decorative frame. Use economical, editable vector construction, not thousands of tiny fragments.

SHARED ART DIRECTION: cohesive restrained engraved fantasy illustration, with expressive connected silhouettes and broad sculptural planes. Three clear value groups, sparse form-following cuts, upper-left light, clean ink contours, quiet negative space. Palette: dark forest ink #172928 background, shadow #334b40, sage #789579, pale cream #dfd4b4, muted copper #b97c5e, restrained warm gold #c5a76a, steel #a9b4aa. Keep species-specific colors: warm gray-brown cub, cool steel mechanical pup, charcoal/copper imp, orange-cream flame, sage/ivory wisp. Natural material colors must remain visible in Golden scenes; avoid turning the whole subject gold. No photorealism, gloss, dense hatching, smooth plastic or noisy gradients. The subjects must remain distinct at 160 by 112 and 80 by 56. Fill roughly 75 percent of each scene; allow generous quiet margins, especially above ears/flames and around paws or shield. Present clear forms before detail.

VARIANTS: a Golden minion is recognizably the SAME unit with a purposeful different gesture and contour. A hue shift, extra glow, larger scale or added frame is insufficient. Give each pair consistent anatomy/material and comparable visual weight while changing the action. A thumbnail viewer should tell normal from Golden even in grayscale.

SQUIRE PAIR (row 1, columns 1 and 2): a small young armored guard in dull steel and asymmetric cloth, shield supported by a clearly connected forearm. Normal: low braced stance, one bent knee, a compact broad shield held near the body, short cloth tail, head turned watchfully. Golden: a higher forward brace with one foot planted ahead, shield raised and angled outward, elbow visibly carrying the shield's weight, a wider answering cloth gesture. Keep shield thickness, neck/shoulder transitions and hand contact readable. Two clear connected arms and legs; no floating shield or detached head. Face simplified, no tiny facial clutter.

CLOCKWORK PUP PAIR (row 1, columns 3 and 4): one compact mechanical dog with a continuous head-neck-chest connection, tapered snout, two angular alert ears, fitted steel plates and selective copper joints. Normal: low curious crouch, nose reaching toward the front, clear near forepaw planted and hindquarters tucked, tail gently countering. Golden: a lively forward spring with one forepaw raised and one planted, opened chest gesture and a fitted copper chest plate. The spine and four-leg anatomy remain believable; far limbs can be quiet and partly hidden. No extra paws, severed legs, human face, skeletal skull or fox-sized long tail. Broad metal planes, minimal seams.

COAL IMP PAIR (row 2, columns 1 and 2): a small charcoal-skinned imp with two short asymmetric horns, a compact torso, bent legs and connected clawed hands. Normal: crouched and guarded, holding one warm coal close to its chest in one hand, the other hand resting on a bent knee; small coal glow. Golden: higher planted stance, both hands extending the same coal outward, shoulders and elbows supporting its weight; a short tail answers the wider gesture. Preserve the imp identity and distinct negative space between arms and torso. Simple face, strong cheek/brow planes; no mouth full of tiny teeth, sprawling flames or disconnected hands.

KINDLE SPARK PAIR (row 2, columns 3 and 4): a small living flame expressed as one connected tapered flame body around a clean dark opening. Normal: compact curling body, one hooked flame crest leaning forward, a quiet lower ember base, cream core and muted orange/copper outer plane. Golden: lifted sweeping flame gesture with a broader dark opening and one clear trailing fork, rising diagonally while remaining one connected flame mass. Different silhouette, not a larger duplicate or just a halo. No humanoid armor, tiny sparks, floating face or separate ornamental ring. Use broad flat flame planes with crisp edges rather than gradients.

BRIAR CUB PAIR (row 3, columns 1 and 2): a young sturdy bear, warm gray-brown coat, rounded ears, short broad muzzle, heavy connected shoulders and compact paws. Normal: low crouch, one leading forepaw extended, rounded back and tucked rear paws, head turned toward the viewer in three-quarter profile. Golden: an alert raised leading paw, head held higher and broad shoulders shifting into a firmer stance; the supporting paw and hind legs visibly carry the weight. The animal is a bear cub, not a wolf, cat, adult bear, stuffed toy or a pile of circles. Keep the muzzle/cheek/neck continuous, simplify fur into a few broad planes, and avoid finger-like toes or extra limbs.

COAL WISP PAIR (row 3, columns 3 and 4): one small curled sage/ivory spirit wrapping around a single dark hollow, with a tapered tail and a distinct directional crest. Normal: a quiet compact sideways curl, asymmetrical broad head-like crest and one smooth tail. Golden: a rising S-shaped sweep with a clearly split trailing tail around the same hollow identity, one leading ivory plane and restrained warm accent. Keep the hollow open and the contour continuous. No humanoid body, skull, disconnected floating dots, glass orb, bright ring or dense glow. Distinguish the wisp's cool flowing shape from the Spark's pointed warm flame.

Deliver twelve coherent finished illustrations. Every cell must be cleanly extractable as a complete 10:7 image, and each normal/Golden pair must show a real readable gesture difference while sharing the same identity and visual style.
